title: Cold Chain
protagonist: Adaeze Okonkwo, District Vaccine Logistics Officer, Gomba District
primary_metric: doses delivered within +2 C to +8 C

options.A: Four AOV ACB-264SL cold boxes ($307.12; 3 on the truck route, 1 on the motorcycle route) meeting every facility's full stated demand
options.B: Two heavy Blowkings CB-20-CF cold boxes ($256.00) fully supplying only the four truck-reachable facilities

balance_test.argument_A: Reaches all six facilities at full stated demand (9,000 doses delivered, zero shortfall); delivers 1,200 more in-spec doses (17.1%). Costs $51.12 more and Nyamirama's 800 doses arrive spoiled regardless -- the box's raw 132.3 h rating is already shorter than the 134 h trip, so no opening-cost assumption saves it.
balance_test.argument_B: 16.6% cheaper ($256.00 vs $307.12), superior thermal performance (SA:V 0.0961 vs 0.1188), 34 h of cold-life slack at the last stop vs Order A's tightest 6.3 h (pre-twist), zero spoilage, and no dependence on a motorcycle run in the rain. Abandons two facilities and 2,000 doses of demand entirely.
balance_test.twist_effect: A nine-hour detour erases Order A's entire margin: in-spec delivery falls from 8,200 to exactly 7,000, a dead tie with Order B. It never falls below B under any tested opening-cost value (see sensitivity_model.py).
balance_test.stability: Stable for opening_cost_h in [2,6]: base margin is 17.1% at every value in that range. The TWIST is only stable for opening_cost_h in [~2.65,6] -- it produces a dead tie for c=3..6h but does nothing at c=2h (Order A keeps its full 17.1% margin; Bulera's twist-day slack is 1.3h). NOT stable with respect to Assumption 2 (in_spec_fraction): -50% flips the base case to a tie (3,950=3,950); +50% widens the margin to 28.6%, breaking the SPEC Section 2 20% cap. See cases/cold-chain/sensitivity_model.py and Guide Notes 'Lessons Learned' for the required facilitator disclosure of both.

assumptions.statement: Order A's four boxes are assigned by vehicle, not by facility: three boxes travel the truck route and serve all four road-accessible facilities between them; one box travels the motorcycle route and serves both Bulera and Nyamirama. Order B's two boxes both travel the truck route. The split of the four truck stops among the three truck boxes does not affect the outcome -- even the worst case (one box absorbing all four stops) still clears the last truck stop with 20.3 h to spare -- so no further convention is needed for the truck leg.
assumptions.why: The case originally left this unstated. A Tier 2 cold-solve probe found that three independent fresh readers each inferred a different box-to-facility assignment and computed three different in-spec totals from the same packet. Stating it explicitly removes the ambiguity rather than leaving readers to guess a convention that was never disclosed.

assumptions.statement: Each lid opening costs 4 hours of cold life, deducted UP FRONT for all planned openings before the trip begins (a box planned to open at two facilities starts at rated cold life minus 8 h).
assumptions.why: WHO certifies cold life with the lid closed for the entire period; no published source gives a per-opening penalty. Verified stable: the case's 17.1% base margin and its tie-under-twist result are unchanged for any value from 2 to 6 hours (see sensitivity_model.py).

assumptions.statement: A container holds +2 to +8 C for its entire rated cold life; warming to +10 C happens quickly once ice is exhausted. Cold life is therefore treated as in-spec time.
assumptions.why: No source publishes a warming curve. Real curves are flat during ice melt then steepen, so this is closer to physical behaviour than linear warming and it removes the +8/+10 ambiguity. It is the optimistic direction and the case says so.

derived.note: computed from Appendix A external dimensions; SA:V falls monotonically as cold life rises across all five containers

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: in_spec_fraction encodes Appendix F Assumption 2's own stated simplification -- 'treat cold life as the in-spec time' -- not a measured or citable figure. The case already discloses in the case text itself that this is the optimistic direction: a real box drifts upward through +8 C somewhat before reaching +10 C, so true in-spec time is shorter than rated cold life. How much shorter depends on the ambient temperature and handling conditions of a specific future trip, which cannot be known in advance -- the same irreducible forecast uncertainty as a future weather or handling-conditions question, not a research gap this case failed to close. At -50% flex the base case flips to an exact tie (3,950 = 3,950 in-spec doses); at +50% flex the margin widens to 28.6%, breaking the SPEC Section 2 20% cap. Both directions are already recorded in balance_test.stability and must stay visible to a facilitator, not eliminated by inventing a false-precision drift curve no public source actually provides for these specific WHO-PQS box models.
